spec.description:
Summary

Fleet managers and dispatch teams need a centralized tool to monitor and manage over 500 vehicles. The fleet management system provides essential features for tracking vehicle status, driver attendance, and location data to support daily operations.

Who it's for

• Fleet managers
• Dispatch teams
• Driver teams
• System administrators
• IT admins
• Finance teams

What it does (first release)

• Track live locations of all vehicles
• Manage driver attendance and schedules
• Set up geo-fencing for vehicle monitoring
• Dispatch vehicles based on current demand
• Monitor vehicle maintenance and asset status
• Provide alerts for maintenance due dates
• Record driver performance metrics
• Generate reports on vehicle usage
• Track fuel consumption for each vehicle
• Manage vehicle assignments to drivers
• Monitor compliance with regulations
• Facilitate communication between drivers and dispatch

Out of scope (for now)

• Integration with third-party software

questions.question: How often should vehicle locations be updated for tracking?
questions.context: More frequent updates provide better visibility but increase costs.

options.label: Every 5 seconds
options.description: Provides real-time tracking but can be costly for data usage.

options.label: Every 30 seconds
options.description: Balances cost and visibility, suitable for most operations.

options.label: Every 1 minute
options.description: Reduces costs but may lag in urgent situations.

options.label: Custom frequency
options.description: Allows flexibility based on specific needs.

questions.question: How should driver attendance be managed?
questions.context: Different methods can impact ease of use and accuracy.

options.label: Manual check-in by drivers
options.description: Simple but relies on driver honesty and can be inaccurate.

options.label: Automated check-in via GPS
options.description: More accurate and reduces manual work, but may raise privacy concerns.

options.label: Biometric check-in (fingerprint/face recognition)
options.description: Highly secure but may require additional hardware.

options.label: Custom method
options.description: Allows for tailored solutions based on specific needs.

questions.question: What should trigger alerts for geo-fencing?
questions.context: Different triggers can impact how proactive the system is.

options.label: Entering or exiting a geo-fenced area
options.description: Provides immediate alerts for better control.

options.label: Exceeding speed limits within the area
options.description: Helps monitor driver behavior but may create alert fatigue.

options.label: Custom trigger conditions
options.description: Allows flexibility for specific operational needs.

questions.question: What should trigger maintenance alerts for vehicles?
questions.context: Different triggers can affect how timely maintenance is addressed.

options.label: Based on mileage
options.description: Standard method, ensures regular maintenance.

options.label: Based on time intervals
options.description: Useful for vehicles that may not accumulate mileage quickly.

options.label: Custom criteria
options.description: Allows for tailored maintenance schedules based on unique needs.

questions.question: How frequently should reports on vehicle usage be generated?
questions.context: Frequency can impact decision-making and resource allocation.

options.label: Daily
options.description: Provides timely insights but may require more resources.

options.label: Weekly
options.description: Balances insight with resource use, suitable for most operations.

options.label: Monthly
options.description: Less frequent, may miss urgent issues but reduces workload.

options.label: Custom frequency
options.description: Allows flexibility based on specific reporting needs.

questions.question: What key metrics should be tracked for driver performance?
questions.context: Choosing the right metrics can help improve overall fleet efficiency.

options.label: Speeding incidents
options.description: Helps identify unsafe driving behavior.

options.label: Fuel efficiency
options.description: Tracks how efficiently drivers use fuel, impacting costs.

options.label: On-time deliveries
options.description: Measures reliability and punctuality, crucial for customer satisfaction.

options.label: Custom metrics
options.description: Allows for tracking of specific performance indicators relevant to your fleet.

improvements.title: Unvalidated Mutation Inputs in api-documentation.ts
improvements.impact: app/actions/api-documentation.ts processes mutations without runtime schema validation (Zod/Valibot). Malformed client inputs or missing fields can trigger runtime crashes or database corruption.
improvements.remediation: Wrap incoming action arguments in a Zod schema validation (e.g. z.object({...}).parse(payload)) before running mutations.

improvements.title: Missing Auth Guard in test-api-settings.ts
improvements.impact: app/actions/test-api-settings.ts appears to execute state mutations without verifying caller session context. In Next.js, Server Actions are public POST endpoints that anyone can invoke directly.
improvements.remediation: Verify session identity at the start of each action handler (e.g. const session = await auth(); if (!session) throw new Error('Unauthorized');).

improvements.title: Missing Root error.tsx Boundary in App Router
improvements.impact: No root error.tsx boundary exists. If a Server Component or action throws an uncaught error, Next.js displays an unstyled server crash page instead of a graceful recovery UI.
improvements.remediation: Create app/error.tsx with a user-friendly error state and a reset() retry trigger.

improvements.title: Missing Loading Skeletons in privacy
improvements.impact: Route segments (privacy) do not define loading.tsx. Users will experience blank screen transitions during slow server fetches.
improvements.remediation: Add loading.tsx with skeleton placeholders in critical route folders to enable instant streaming transitions.

improvements.title: Deprecated middleware.ts in Next.js 16 (Rename to proxy.ts)
improvements.impact: Next.js 16 deprecates the middleware.ts naming convention in favor of proxy.ts for network-level request boundaries.
improvements.remediation: Rename middleware.ts to proxy.ts and update config matcher rules to ensure seamless runtime compatibility.

improvements.title: Next.js 15+ Async Request APIs (cookies & headers)
improvements.impact: Next.js 15 makes cookies(), headers(), and route params asynchronous. Synchronous access triggers runtime deprecation warnings and will fail in future releases.
improvements.remediation: Audit server components and server actions to ensure cookies() and headers() calls are preceded with await.
